title: Maronite Qurbono: bounded manuscript and printed-book stages

traditions.label: Maronite Antiochene Qurbono
traditions.scope: Maronite Eucharistic books in Syriac and native Syriac/Arabic composition; independent vernacular translation history excluded.
traditions.coverage_note: First printing through 2005 with a bounded manuscript precursor and 2003-2006 synodal reception prescriptions. Dates mark attestation/publication/approval, not continuous use. The 2005 stage rests on a reproduced decree and an approved translation; the Arabic/Syriac original remains an acquisition gap.

sources.title: Missale Chaldaicum iuxta ritum Ecclesiae nationis Maronitarum (Rome, Medici, 1592/1594)
sources.inspection: Whole 300-page PDF acquired. Page images inspected: PDF 5 Latin title; PDF 7–8 dedication; PDF 9 Syriac title and Latin 1592 imprint; PDF 10–14 opening liturgical body; PDF 295 final Syriac page; PDF 296 Latin colophon and examiner statement.
sources.limitations: Identity and Latin paratext checked visually. Syriac body not transcribed, repertoire not independently enumerated, and possible in-sheet variants not collated. No 1608 Du Perron preface found in inspected preliminaries. Filename ending 1594-1608 is a precautionary scratch filename, not a bibliographic conclusion.

sources.title: Pierre Jabbour, L’identité religieuse des Maronites du Mont-Liban au XVIe siècle au prisme du premier missel maronite imprimé à Rome, Proche-Orient Chrétien 70 (2020), 59–87
sources.inspection: Author-uploaded rendered full text read: pp 59–65 identity and divided manuscripts; pp 70–75 institution and epiclesis alterations; pp 76–78 variant 1608 copies. Journal abstract checked at https://journals.usj.edu.lb/poc/article/view/1200 ; DOI 10.3917/poc.701.0059.
sources.limitations: Rendered author text has damaged character mapping. PDF page-image download was unavailable; quoted Syriac not used as checked transcription. Manuscripts and variant 1608 copies not independently inspected. This is original research describing its own collation, not a collation performed here.

sources.title: BnF catalogue: Missale Chaldaicum, Romae 1594[-1608], RES M-B-3
sources.inspection: Full catalogue notice read: publication, extent, notes on reimpression, changed text and Du Perron Latin/Syriac preface dated 1608.
sources.limitations: Catalogue only; specific copy not scanned here. Syriac title retaining 1592 does not make this an unmodified 1592 witness.

sources.title: Pierre Dib, Maronite (Église), Dictionnaire de théologie catholique 10.1 (1928), columns 129–130
sources.inspection: Both columns 129–130 read on the scanned page image, especially the missal paragraphs. Publication/authorship corroborated by Raymond Janin’s 1928 review metadata at https://www.persee.fr/doc/rebyz_1146-9447_1928_num_27_151_4685_t1_0376_0000_3 .
sources.limitations: Historical synthesis, not inspected 1716 or 1763 book. Wikimedia filename 1908 is not this volume’s publication year. Gives nine anaphoras for 1762–63, conflicting with official 1992 introduction’s eight. Describes later Gospel additions without a fully verified first-edition locus.

sources.title: Seely J. Beggiani, The Divine Liturgy of the Maronite Church: History and Commentary, second revised edition (Saint Maron Publications, 1998)
sources.inspection: PDF images checked: PDF 1–3 title, edition, copyright/imprimatur; printed 18–21 (PDF 24–27), section The Maronite Missal. ISBN1-885589-07-7.
sources.limitations: Modern copyrighted scholarship downloaded for scratch research only; no text or scan proposed for repository retention. Historical summary rather than direct 1716/1763/1888/1973 collation. Identifies distinct 1972 and 1973 experiments, unlike the compressed official retrospective.

sources.title: Seely J. Beggiani, Aspects of Maronite History, Part Eight
sources.inspection: Sections Liturgical Developments and The Mysteries read, including 1716 changes and 1736/1755–56 norms.
sources.limitations: Online historical essay. Its statement that no edition followed 1736 before 1816 omits 1763; not used to establish publication sequence. No primary page or exact rubrical wording supplied for the relocation of ablutions.

sources.title: Ketābā de-qurbānā āk ʿeyādā de-ʿidtā d-Antiukiyā de-Mārūnāye, Beirut 1908, second printing
sources.inspection: Bonn bibliographic record read. Existing retained PDF images checked: whole-file PDF 441 title, PDF 436–440 front matter, PDF 8 calendar/computus table. PDF 441 = retained second part local 218. Added 2026-10-21: anaphora section headings viewed at 300 dpi on whole-file PDF 352 (Roman Church, Syriac with Garshuni parallel heading), 330 (Peter, head of the Apostles, Syriac with Garshuni), 318 (Twelve holy Apostles), 310 (Mark), 292 (John, apostle and evangelist), 279 (Xystus), 264 (Eustathius) and 255 (John Maron, patriarch of Antioch); institution narratives in large type on PDF 347, 327, 316, 306, 289, 276, 262 and 251; Garshuni preface headed al-muqaddima on PDF 439; a first part with readings and an index by months (PDF 11-12).
sources.limitations: Title and preface images examined; no checked Syriac/Garshuni transcription or translation. Repertoire/order claims below come from named scholarship, not this visual inspection. The file called 1908-contents.png is a calendar table, not an anaphora contents list. The 2026-10-21 roster is a heading-level reading in reversed PDF order; printed page numbers were not relied on and the preface was not transcribed.

sources.title: Biblioteca Apostolica Vaticana, Vat.sir.431 (digitized manuscript)
sources.inspection: Provider image 46 of 67 (acquired whole by the 2026-10-19 lane) viewed on 2026-10-21: the opening with the leaf foliated 45 in Western numerals. Two Syriac passages of the post-institution invocation are encircled in ink with interlinear and marginal marks, and a Latin marginal note of a later hand explains the invocation of the Holy Spirit to make this bread the body of Christ, says that some over-zealous persons removed it, and defends it from the liturgies of Clement, Basil, Chrysostom and James, the Council of Florence and Bellarmine, De sacramento Eucharistiae book 4 chapter 14.
sources.limitations: One opening viewed; the Syriac text was not transcribed and the Latin note was read only in outline (its wording about removal is a tentative reading). The note's citation of Bellarmine places it no earlier than his treatise; the hand is not dated here. Other folios of Vat.sir.431 and the Florence parts of manuscript O were not inspected.

sources.inspection: Complete introductory account read, especially First Edition, Succeeding Editions, Current Project, Liturgical Year, Scripture Readings, Western Syriac Anaphora, Eastern Syriac Anaphora of Sharar, and Six Anaphoras of the New Text; dated signature read.
sources.limitations: Contemporary primary reform explanation for 1992, retrospective for older books. English translation inspected, not 1992 Syriac/Arabic book or its decree. No protected liturgical text imported. The 1992 book is not asserted to be the latest edition.

Assemani dated 10 April 1763; canvas 363 Imprimatur leaf; anaphora headings in red Serto on canvases 226, 196, 183, 156, 137, 116, 103 and 094, each followed by its institution narrative in large type (canvases 221/220, 192/191, 177/176, 152/151, 133/132, 113/112, 101/100, 089/088); running heads of canvases 040-416; Good Friday heading on canvas 072; Garshuni printer's note on canvas 4. Entry Ms. orient. 6 (Kaufhold pp. 108f): a defective copy of the Rome 1716 Propaganda Fide Missale Syriacum with Syriac and Garshuni manuscript supplements; surviving anaphoras with printed page ranges.

sources.limitations: Bibliographic digest of Feulner's OCA 260 article, read in its text layer only. Gives anaphora counts and selected page loci; it does not list the 1716 roster by name and is not a collation.

sources.inspection: PDF page 1552 contents list of the anaphoras read in the bilingual text layer on 2026-10-21 (English and Arabic titles with page numbers 754-897); the prior cold reviewer viewed the page image.

stages.label: Manuscript O before Roman editing
stages.scope: Source manuscript identified by Jabbour, including the pre-editing institution and epiclesis layers; not all precursors of the print.
stages.witness_label: Mikhail al-Rizzi’s manuscript O: Florence BNCF Cl.III.79 and Cl.III.74, with Vatican Vat.sir.431; colophon BNCF Cl.III.74 f 154r–v.
stages.summary: A divided 1566 missal used in preparing the first print; supplements also contributed.

evidence.claim: Reassembles gatherings of O across the three shelfmarks; the print also uses other material.

The Vatican part of the reconstructed manuscript shows encircled invocation passages and a Latin marginal note on the epiclesis on the folio Jabbour cites (f. 45r); the marked Syriac was not transcribed, so its correspondence to Jabbour's correction layers is not checked here.

stages.limitations: Reconstruction attributed to Jabbour; surviving manuscripts and colophon not inspected. It is not a complete uncontested single-parent genealogy. 2026-10-21: one Vatican opening (f. 45) was inspected; the Florence parts and the colophon remain uninspected.
stages.reception: Maronite manuscript provenance; date of its dispatch to Rome is disputed. The later printed uniform formula must not be projected back over all manuscript layers.

stages.label: First print with revised institution and epicleses
stages.scope: Roman first printing, bounded by checked paratext and source-described liturgical revision.
stages.witness_label: Missale Chaldaicum iuxta ritum Ecclesiae nationis Maronitarum, Romae in Typographia Medicea; IA bub_gb_5Eqy8WGF9aQC.
stages.summary: Fourteen anaphoras; Sixtus first and Sharar included. Institution wording standardized; epiclesis petitions altered.

evidence.claim: Latin 1594 and Syriac 1592 dates coexist in this physical witness; 1594 dedication and examiner colophon are visible.
Describes fourteen anaphoras and alteration of institution and epiclesis.
Identifies Sixtus first and the inclusion of Sharar.

stages.limitations: Liturgical body not transcribed or collated. Dual title dates do not establish two successive textual states.
stages.reception: Dib reports introduction at the 1596 synod with Dandini. Beggiani records initial prohibition and later permission while manuscript formulas continued locally; neither account proves universal immediate replacement.

stages.label: Reprint variant replacing commemorated names
stages.scope: Specific diptych/commemoration revision in Jabbour’s beta group; not every 1608 copy.
stages.witness_label: Missale Chaldaicum 1608 reimpressions, beta group in Jabbour’s comparison; BnF RES M-B-3 is a separately identified 1608 reissue, not assigned here to beta.
stages.summary: One 1608 group substitutes Maron, Antony, Jacob and Ephrem for earlier commemorated names.

evidence.claim: Distinguishes alpha copies marking names from beta copies substituting them.
Confirms a 1608 reimpression with textual changes and new Du Perron preface.

stages.limitations: No 1608 copy independently collated. Jabbour warns that editions may be impressions; alpha/beta is his analytical grouping, not a new universal liturgical edition.
stages.reception: Presence in surviving copies establishes a printed variant; no community-wide reception date established.

stages.label: Roman-derived anaphora and Good Friday adaptation
stages.scope: Second Roman missal revision described in multiple histories.
stages.witness_label: Missale Syriacum iuxta ritum Ecclesiae Antiochenae nationis Maronitarum, Rome, Propaganda Fide 1716.
stages.summary: Fourteen anaphoras remain according to Dib (Feulner counts thirteen), but the roster changes: Roman Church added; Sharar removed as an anaphora and adapted for Good Friday.

evidence.claim: Reports altered roster, fourteen total, Roman Church and Sharar-derived Good Friday order.
Explains adaptation of Roman Canon material to the structure of Twelve Apostles.

stages.limitations: No 1716 page images or complete roster inspected. The Roman Church anaphora should not be described merely as an unchanged translation of the Roman Canon. The total is disputed: Dib and the 1992 introduction give fourteen, Feulner (maronite-feulner-klampfl2008) thirteen; neither count is adopted as settled.
stages.reception: Publication and later reception are distinct. Synodal debates about institution wording do not independently identify a new missal state.

stages.label: Reduced anaphora repertoire
stages.date_label: 1762 title imprint; approbation 10 April 1763 (same copy); 1763 in the official introduction
stages.scope: Third Roman edition with smaller repertoire; disputed exact count retained.
stages.witness_label: Missale Syriacum juxta ritum Ecclesiae Antiochenae nationis Syrorum Maronitarum, Rome, Komarek 1762 (approbation 10 April 1763); ONB 22.D.32 ALT PRUNK.
stages.summary: Repertoire reduced from the 1716 book. The inspected copy carries eight anaphora headings, each with its own institution narrative: Peter head of the Apostles, Twelve Apostles, Xystus, John, Mark, Eustathius, the holy Roman Church and John Maron. A separate Good Friday order headed as the anaphora of the signing of the holy chalice follows them. Dib and Beggiani count nine; the 1992 introduction counts eight.

evidence.locus: Canvas 430 title; canvas 3 approbation; anaphora headings canvases 226, 196, 183, 156, 137, 116, 103, 094; Good Friday heading canvas 072 with running heads 040-071
evidence.claim: Title 1762 and approbation 1763 stand on one copy; the book has eight anaphoras with institution narratives and a separately headed Good Friday chalice-signing order.
Dates third edition 1762–63 and counts nine.
Counts nine and identifies first anaphora as Second Peter.
Reports eight for 1763.

stages.limitations: Eight anaphoras plus the Good Friday item are what the inspected copy contains. That a count of nine includes the Good Friday item is compatible with this but is not stated by Dib or Beggiani, so it is not adopted as their reason. The approbation says the book was collated with the 1716 Propaganda missal and agrees with it; that is a doctrinal approval formula, not evidence that the repertoire was unchanged. Body text not transcribed; one copy, variant issues unchecked; the canvas 4 printer's date is unread.
stages.reception: Subsequent Lebanese printings are reported; continuity of every wording or rubric has not been collated.

stages.label: Dibs order with Roman Church first
stages.scope: Dibs’s reorder, witnessed bibliographically by 1888 and 1908; no separate 1908 revision established.
stages.witness_label: Yusuf al-Dibs, Beirut missal 1888; Ketābā de-qurbānā, al-Maṭbaʿa al-Mārūnīya 1908, second printing.
stages.summary: Roman Church replaces Peter at the head of the anaphora sequence; the 1908 printing has the same eight anaphoras as 1762 in a new order.

evidence.claim: Second Peter leads the preceding edition; Debs 1888 places Roman Church first.
Identifies the 1908 second printing and its retained title page.
Order in the 1908 printing: Roman Church, Peter, Twelve Apostles, Mark, John, Xystus, Eustathius, John Maron.

stages.limitations: 1888 itself not seen; 1888/1908 differences uncollated. The 1908 order is a witness to the Dibs line and cannot by itself show which reorderings Dibs made in 1888 and which came from intervening Qozhaya printings or from the 1908 second printing itself. 1888 date is revision attestation, not the duration of use.
stages.reception: The 1908 printing is a witness to the Dibs line; it is not counted as a separately proved reform.

stages.label: Roman experimental proposal
stages.scope: A proposal described by Beggiani, requiring identification of its exact text and enactment.
stages.witness_label: Experimental text proposed by the Congregation for the Eastern Churches; exact 1972 book identity not inspected.
stages.summary: One-year experiment containing Twelve Apostles alone.

evidence.claim: Separates 1972 Roman proposal from the 1973 patriarchal experiment.

stages.limitations: Book and authorization document missing. Deliberately provisional; cannot be merged automatically with 1973.
stages.reception: Proposal and authorized local adoption require separate evidence.

stages.label: Patriarchal experimental simple rite
stages.scope: Experimental simple rite; full institution text and relation to 1972 remain unchecked.
stages.witness_label: Simple Rite issued by the Maronite Patriarchate in 1973, described by the 1992 introduction.
stages.summary: A restricted experimental book; the official introduction reports one anaphora.

evidence.claim: Identifies 1973 Simple Rite as a one-anaphora experiment.
Identifies a distinct 1973 patriarchal text retaining Roman institution wording.

evidence.locus: PDF 6 (2005 patriarchal introduction, English; the Arabic counterpart follows)
evidence.claim: The revision proposed by the Liturgical Commission was approved by Patriarch Meouchi with the consent of the patriarchal synod, as an abbreviated ritual put into effect by decree 43/1973 of 13 April 1973 for one year as an experiment.

stages.limitations: No original 1973 book or decree inspected; the decree number and date come from a later patriarchal introduction reproduced in 2012. Exact identity of the single anaphora is not safely supplied from Beggiani's description of 1972.
stages.reception: Experimental permission is not perpetual universal promulgation. Neither source establishes identical local reception everywhere.

stages.label: Reformed six-anaphora Qurbono
stages.scope: Syriac/Arabic reform represented by the contemporary commission introduction and later commentary.
stages.witness_label: Book of Offering according to the Tradition of the Antiochene Syriac Maronite Church, Bkerke 1992.
stages.summary: Six anaphoras: Twelve Apostles, Peter, James, John, Mark, Sixtus; expanded annual services.

evidence.locus: Western Syriac Anaphora; Six Anaphoras; Liturgical Year
evidence.claim: Describes revised structure, shared institution wording and expanded services.
Confirms six names, Twelve Apostles first, and patriarchal promulgation.

stages.limitations: Primary reform explanation, not a full transcription. Comprehensive Old/New Testament lectionary was still being prepared; later complementary Gospel/Epistle books are not successive missal versions.
stages.reception: Intro reports synodal/Congregation approval and patriarchal signature. 31 July dates the introduction, not independently the decree or universal effective date. A later 2005 edition is reported by Jabbour; 1992 is not labelled current.

stages.label: Second edition of the revised Qurbono with eight anaphoras
stages.date_label: 2005; patriarchal decree 29 June 2005, in use from the first Sunday of November 2005
stages.scope: Patriarchal approval of the revised Mass book called its second edition; structure known from the reproduced decree, introduction and the approved 2012 translation, not from the Arabic/Syriac original.
stages.witness_label: Kitab al-Quddas according to the rite of the Antiochene Syriac Maronite Church, Bkerke 2005 (seminary library Tl 188 Ar, 1117 pp.), read through the 2012 approved English edition.
stages.summary: Decree 1512/2005 approves the new edition after the Congregation for the Eastern Churches' letter 381/2003 of 17 April 2005 and synodal consent, orders its use from the first Sunday of November 2005 and forbids any other Mass book from 25 December 2005. Eight anaphoras: Twelve Apostles, Peter, James, John, Mark, Xystus, John Chrysostom and John Maron.

evidence.claim: Approval chain, effective and exclusive-use dates, and the description of the book as the second edition of the revised ritual.
The edition translated from Bkerke 2005 has eight anaphoras with the names listed.

stages.limitations: Arabic/Syriac 2005 book not acquired; decree and contents are read in a later approved translation. The introduction does not name the first edition; equating it with the 1992 book is an inference left open. Anaphora names do not show whether texts of the same name match earlier printings.
stages.reception: The decree prescribes use throughout the patriarchal territory and the diaspora from November 2005 and exclusive use from 25 December 2005; actual uniform use is not established. The 2003-2006 synod separately requires the approved Mass order.

stages.label: Synodal book-use and celebration prescriptions
stages.scope: Eucharistic legislation governing approved books and celebration; a reception witness alongside printed missals.
stages.witness_label: Maronite Patriarchal Synod, Text 12: Liturgy, official Arabic text on Bkerki.org
stages.summary: The synod directs exclusive use of the Mass order approved by the synod and patriarchal decree, alongside separately issued Epistle and Gospel books, chant book and ritual directions. It prefers concelebration at the principal altar, prescribes the Presanctified on Good Friday and no Mass on Holy Saturday.

evidence.locus: Sacraments chapter, section 2, القدّاس أو الإفخارستيّا, first eight paragraphs; final recommendation 5
evidence.claim: Explicitly distinguishes the approved Mass order from complementary reading, chant and directions books; sets celebration and Holy Week prescriptions.

stages.limitations: No new complete missal recension is inferred from the synodal date. The before-state and first introduction of these rubrics are not established here; no revision edge is drawn.
stages.reception: The synodal directions encompass the patriarchal territory and diaspora in the document’s account of the liturgical commission. Prescribed unity does not establish uniform empirical use.

transitions.summary: Roman preparation standardized institution wording and changed epiclesis petitions.

changes.locus_before: Manuscript O and its correction layers; not independently collated.
changes.locus_after: Printed anaphoras; complete loci not checked.

evidence.claim: Studies successive manuscript corrections and printed uniformization.

changes.after: Revised petitions concerning sacramental benefit to communicants.
changes.locus_before: O, including Vat.sir.431 f 45r, as analyzed by Jabbour.

evidence.claim: Examines crossed-out layers and edited epicleses.
Describes the changed object of the epiclesis and residual older wording.
Encircled invocation passages and a Latin marginal defence of the epiclesis are visible on the folio Jabbour cites.
Supplies a manuscript reconstruction and bounded examples of editing.

transitions.limitations: Manuscript ancestry remains a scholarly reconstruction with supplementary sources. No direct before/after Syriac collation was performed. Do not attribute all changes solely to an editor on the strength of the approval colophon. 2026-10-21: the before-side folio Vat.sir.431 f. 45 was viewed, but the markings were not transcribed or collated against the print.

transitions.summary: A 1608 variant replaces selected commemorated names.

changes.before: Philoxenus, Patra, Anthymus and Jacob in the earlier set.
changes.after: Maron, Antony, Jacob and Ephrem in the beta set.
changes.locus_after: 1608 beta-group commemoration; physical-copy locus not verified here.

evidence.claim: Distinguishes substitution in beta from marking in alpha.
A modified 1608 reimpression is independently catalogued.

transitions.limitations: Specific impression/copy relationship is attributed, not proven by our scan. Do not generalize beta readings to all 1608 copies or assert BnF RES M-B-3 is beta.

transitions.summary: The roster changes while retaining fourteen: Roman Church enters and Sharar becomes a Good Friday adaptation.

changes.after: Sharar omitted as an anaphora; Roman Church added.

evidence.claim: Describes replacements, insertion and unchanged total.

changes.before: Sharar anaphora in the first printed missal.
changes.after: Its prayers adapted to a Good Friday presanctified order.
changes.locus_before: 1592–94 Sharar; original page not independently checked.
changes.locus_after: 1716 Good Friday order; original page not independently checked.

evidence.claim: Explains adaptation rather than recovery of the older Lenten presanctified service.
Attributes the relocation to 1716.
Explicit comparison of the first and second printed editions.

transitions.limitations: Exact 1716 text and full roster not inspected. Edge compares documented states; intermediate 1608 variants are not silently treated as its exclusive parent. The unchanged total of fourteen is Dib's; Feulner counts fourteen for 1592-94 but thirteen for 1716, so the total after the change is unresolved.

transitions.summary: The anaphora repertoire contracts; exact resulting count is disputed.

changes.before: Fourteen anaphoras as counted by Dib and the 1992 introduction; Feulner counts thirteen for 1716, and the total is unresolved.
changes.after: Eight anaphoras with institution narratives (Peter, Twelve Apostles, Xystus, John, Mark, Eustathius, Roman Church, John Maron) plus a Good Friday chalice-signing order headed as an anaphora; Dib/Beggiani count nine, the official introduction eight.

evidence.claim: Reports fourteen to nine.
Reports fourteen to eight.

evidence.locus: West Syriac edition list; section 2.2, Anzahl
evidence.claim: Counts thirteen anaphoras for Rome 1716, against Dib's fourteen.
Roster of the inspected 1762/1763 copy.

changes.before: Scholarship places the anaphoras of James the brother of the Lord and of Matthew the Shepherd among the surviving sections of a defective 1716 copy (Kaufhold), and the anaphora of John Chrysostom at pp. 332-337 of the 1716 edition (Feulner/Klampfl).
changes.after: No heading for James, Matthew the Shepherd or John Chrysostom in the 1762/1763 copy.
changes.locus_before: Münster UB Ms. orient. 6 (Rome 1716): James pp. 182-207, Matthew the Shepherd pp. 250-263 (Kaufhold 1988 pp. 108f); John Chrysostom pp. 332-337 (Feulner/Klampfl).
changes.locus_after: ONB copy, heading canvases 226-094 and running heads 040-416.

evidence.claim: Lists the surviving anaphoras of a defective 1716 copy with page ranges.

evidence.locus: Section 2.2, no. 6 Anaphora des Johannes Chrysostomus
evidence.claim: Cites the Rome 1716 missal, pp. 332-337, for the Chrysostom anaphora.
These three anaphoras are absent from the inspected copy's headings.
Independently reports nine.

transitions.limitations: Reduction is documented despite the disputed count; the 1716 side rests on scholarship (Dib, Kaufhold, Feulner) and the 1716 book was not inspected. The list of removed anaphoras is partial: the Münster copy lacks pages. 1762/1763 are source-reported date bounds, not an inferred period of validity.

transitions.summary: Dibs moves Roman Church to the first position.

changes.before: Peter (head of the Apostles) first; Roman Church seventh of eight.
changes.locus_before: 1762/1763 ONB copy canvases 226 (Peter) and 103 (Roman Church); pre-Dibs sequence described in Beggiani p 19.
changes.locus_after: 1908 printing of the Dibs line, whole-file PDF 352 (Roman Church) and 330 (Peter); 1888 sequence described in Beggiani p 20.

evidence.claim: Explicitly identifies the first anaphora before and after.
Peter heads the 1762/1763 roster and Roman Church is seventh.
Roman Church heads the 1908 roster, followed by Peter.

changes.before: Order Peter, Twelve Apostles, Xystus, John, Mark, Eustathius, Roman Church, John Maron.
changes.after: Order Roman Church, Peter, Twelve Apostles, Mark, John, Xystus, Eustathius, John Maron; same eight names.

evidence.claim: Earlier order.
Later order.
Identifies the named reorder.

transitions.limitations: Intervening Qozhaya printings 1816, 1838, 1855, 1872 and the 1888 book were not seen. Beggiani attributes Roman-first to Dibs 1888; the other moves (Xystus, Mark/John) are observed between the 1762 and 1908 witnesses and may have arisen in any intervening printing. The second change rests on the 1908 witness alone: the transition's 1888 endpoint does not date those moves, which could postdate 1888 if the 1908 second printing altered the order. Heading-level comparison only; no claim of identical wording.

transitions.summary: The experimental simple rite limits the book to one anaphora.

changes.before: Several anaphoras in the Dibs line.
changes.after: One anaphora in the 1973 Simple Rite.
changes.locus_after: 1973 Simple Rite described by the 1992 introduction.

evidence.claim: Attributes one-anaphora scope to 1973.
Explicitly distinguishes the experiment from earlier editions.

transitions.limitations: Source-described comparison, not a claim of direct textual parentage. 1972 Roman proposal and 1973 patriarchal text must still be compared.

transitions.summary: The 1992 reform revises the anaphora structure and selects six anaphoras.

changes.before: Repeated Eastern prayers within the Western structure.
changes.locus_before: Earlier editions collectively described in 1992 introduction.
changes.locus_after: 1992 order described by its commission chairman.

evidence.claim: Identifies removal of duplicated Eastern material.

changes.before: Roman Church first; earlier Roman-derived institution formula.
changes.after: Twelve Apostles first; shared institution wording based on that anaphora.
changes.locus_before: Dibs order; earlier formula described by Beggiani/Dib.
changes.locus_after: 1992 Six Anaphoras of the New Text.

evidence.locus: Six Anaphoras of the New Text
evidence.claim: Explains the new common formula.
Confirms changed order and six-name selection.

evidence.locus: Western Syriac Anaphora; Six Anaphoras; Liturgical Year
evidence.claim: Contemporary account explains the reform’s contents.

transitions.limitations: The 1992 side is a contemporary primary description; the earlier side is a scholarly retrospective. The edge uses their lowest shared evidence level. No paired textual collation was performed. Sharar restoration and a twenty-four-anaphora collection were future projects, not accomplished 1992 contents.

transitions.summary: The second edition adds the anaphoras of John Chrysostom and John Maron to the six of 1992.

changes.before: Six anaphoras: Twelve Apostles, Peter, James, John, Mark, Xystus.
changes.after: Eight anaphoras: the same six plus John Chrysostom and John Maron.
changes.locus_before: 1992 introduction, Western Syriac Anaphora (the six listed as they appear in the book), taken up under Six Anaphoras of the New Text.
changes.locus_after: 2012 edition according to Bkerke 2005, PDF 1552 (printed p. 753) contents.

evidence.locus: Western Syriac Anaphora; Six Anaphoras of the New Text
evidence.claim: Names the six 1992 anaphoras.
Names the eight anaphoras of the edition translated from 2005.
The 2005 book is the approved second edition of the revised ritual.

transitions.limitations: Both sides are official descriptions (a contemporary introduction and an approved translation's contents), not the Arabic/Syriac books. The 2005 introduction does not name 1992 as its first edition. Names alone do not show whether the 2005 John Maron and Chrysostom texts match those of earlier printings.
